page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a third-generation storage-optimized instance powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, presenting 4 vCPUs to the Xen hypervisor. The instance is allocated 30.0 GB of memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per core. A key feature of this server configuration is the inclusion of 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

In synthetic benchmarks, the processing capabilities of the Intel Broadwell architecture show clear age-related constraints. Benchmark results place single-core and multi-core CPU scores from stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark in the lower performance brackets. Memory bandwidth measurements indicate throughput of 157.88 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 22.62 GB/sec for large uncached read operations. The primary strength of the instance lies in its direct-attached NVMe storage density rather than raw CPU execution speeds, as evidenced by Redis SET throughput of 2.54 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 2.81 GB/sec.

The i3.xlarge instance offers a cost-effective resource density profile for workloads requiring localized, low-latency disk I/O paired with moderate RAM without needing top-tier CPU clock speeds. Given the balance of 30 GB RAM and 950 GB local NVMe storage against modest compute scores, this instance is suited for relational and non-relational database hosting, transactional caching layers, log indexing, and data processing tasks dependent on high-speed local disk operations.

The server provides 30.0 GB of memory and includes a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic CPU and memory benchmarks place compute performance in lower percentiles, reflecting its legacy Broadwell hardware foundation. However, the hardware assembly excels at providing dedicated local SSD capacity and moderate RAM density without relying on virtualized network storage. The qualitative value profile favors workloads where disk throughput and local storage latency are prioritized over heavy CPU-bound processing. Consequently, the instance fits database hosting, caching nodes, search indexing, and log analytics tasks.
